title: A Flock of 750,000 Starlings Moves as One. Here's the Trick

scenes.text: Seven hundred and fifty thousand birds can turn at the same moment.
These are starlings, and this is called a murmuration.
Each bird watches only its seven closest neighbors.
When one turns, the signal races through the flock.
In a flock of 400, it crosses in about half a second.
There is no leader. Just seven neighbors.

description:
750,000 birds can turn at the same moment.
Starlings in a murmuration each follow about seven neighbors, and a turn can cross a 400-bird flock in half a second.
Have you ever watched one?
first_comment: No leader, just seven neighbors. What else in nature works like that?
